newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil chief may move to central bank.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil chief may move to central bank.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper said the head of the state oil company Ecopetrol was among possible candidates to fill two upcoming vacancies on the board of directors of Colombia's central bank.

Samper, who spoke in an interview published Thursday in Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper, said the names of his appointees to the bank would be announced next week. But he confirmed widespread rumors that Ecopetrol chief Luis Bernardo Florez was among his top candidates.
"Luis Bernardo is someone who has been very close to the (government's) economic team," Samper said.

"He's very capable and certainly among the possible picks," he added, stressing nonetheless that Florez was just one of "six or seven" candidates to fill the vacancies on the seven-member board when two of its co-directors step down due to obligatory retirement next month.

Ecopetrol spokesmen could not be reached for immediate comment on who might replace Florez as the head of the company that provides the bulk of Colombia's export revenues. He was appointed to the post by Samper just last year after serving as one of the president's top economic advisers.

Central bank sources have played down fears that Samper, who has already named one other member to the board of the Banco de la Republica, could tip the scale in favor of looser monetary policy by naming two other members next month.
"We don't expect the government to name anyone but serious economists to the board," one bank official said.

Samper has pledged to press for a cut in interest rates as part of an emergency economic package announced Monday, however. And since the finance minister is a co-director of the central bank, a majority of its members will soon owe their positions to Samper.
